Quick summary (shareable):

- Cross-border safeguards: We can provide DPF-compatible controls: SCCs execution as controller-processor appendix, contractual DPA annex, SOC2 Type II report, pen-test summary, and detailed encryption/KMS controls. - KMS/BYOK: Supported for Private customers and Dedicated customers via customer-managed KMS integrations. BYOK for hosted tenants is available with HSM-backed key wrapping on request (scope to be agreed in annex).
- Subprocessors: the registry is attached and we will provide per-subprocessor technical evidence within 5 business days after you sign the DPA annex.

Attachments: redwood_dpf_evidence_summary.pdf, subprocessor_registry.csv, dpa-annex-draft-novaera.docx (draft).

Claire / team —

Adding the technical annex you requested. Below are the core technical controls and implementation notes you can include in your RFP response summary.

1) Network & transport
- All customer traffic is TLS 1.3 between client and edge. Internal service-to-service uses mTLS with mutual cert rotation.

2) Data-at-rest
- Persistent stores (logs, metrics, config) use AES-256-GCM encryption at rest. Disk-level encryption and KMS-wrapped volume keys.

3) KMS / key custody
- Hosted: Redwood-managed KMS by default (AWS KMS/Google Cloud KMS).
- Dedicated/Private: BYOK supported via customer KMS and HSM integration (AWS CloudHSM/CloudKMS, Azure Key Vault HSM-backed).
- Key wrapping: we support envelope encryption; customer-managed root keys can be required for decryption of log archives.

4) Caching / model context
- KV cache is kept in-memory and optionally persisted in an encrypted cache for warm-up. Default persisted cache retention is 24 hours; can be reduced to 0 (no persistence) by configuration for sensitive workloads.

5) Logs and telemetry
- Request metadata (timestamps, route, model id) retained by default 30 days. Request payloads and model outputs are redacted in exported logs unless explicitly requested for debugging; data minimization is configurable.
- DSAR workflow: we provide APIs for search/export and deletion of request data; full purge timelines depend on export windows but are contractually defined in the DPA annex.

6) Cross-border transfer rationale (recommended approach)
- Primary option: SCCs executed in the DPA annex + DPF technical measures (encryption, BYOK, limited persistence) and contractual commitments (subprocessor audit rights) — this is the standard approach for hosted product.
- Alternative for highest-assurance: Dedicated capacity with region locking or Private deployment (customer-managed VPC) so data never leaves region or is controlled by customer keys.

7) Audit evidence
- SOC2 Type II report (most recent), pen test executive summary (last 12 months), dataflow diagrams, subprocessor assurance statements. We will provide these upon DPA signature and standard NDA if required.

8) Escape hatches & operational playbook
- If a transfer justification becomes legally constrained, Redwood offers: (a) fast-track region-locking of Dedicated pools, (b) migration assistance to Private deployment, (c) temporary suppression of persistence and extended logging redaction until onboarding completes.

If you want, we can produce a one-page MAP with milestones: DPA signature -> evidence pack delivery (5 business days) -> subprocessor deep-dive (10 business days) -> legal sign-off.

Regards,

Sr. Product Manager, Security & Compliance
